items.abstract: <jats:p>Systemic risk in interbank networks is very difficult to quantify and explain. Current approaches produce either opaque risk scores with no justification, or explanations not relating to the underlying model scores. AttentionRisk-GNN, a graph neural network framework, is introduced in this paper to address both limitations simultaneously. The architecture performs multihead attention on directed exposure graphs, whereby rather than adding explainability to the model after-the-fact, it takes Shapley attribution during the forward pass such that each risk score is provided with a list of the counterparty that actually caused it, ranked. On the 500-node benchmark, the model has F1 = 0.91 and AUC = 0.96, outperforming DebtRank and the three GNN baselines. The runtime scales linearly with respect to the number of institutions on sparse graphs and convergence is guaranteed by standard nonconvex stochastic gradient descent theory.</jats:p>
